claim: At 600 nm the quantum efficiency carried for the Photometrics Kinetix22 is 0.96, and it is not the Kinetix22's own figure: it is one point of the Kinetix's datasheet graph, read off by eye, borrowed as a one-time exception authorised by the person on 2026-08-19.

numbers.name: quantum_efficiency
numbers.note: the 600 nm point of the borrowed curve, which is tabulated on a coarse grid from 200 to 1100 nm. `order_of_magnitude` is declared deliberately: the curve was read off a printed graph by eye and the source marks it `qe_verified: false`, so two decimals are what was written down and not what is known. 600 nm is the grid point beside the band this path collects; any other tabulated point can be filed on request, and none of them is measured here.

validity_conditions: ONE POINT, NOT A CURVE, AND THE NAME SAYS SO NOW. This entry was filed as `camera_qe_curve_is_the_kinetix_graph` earlier today and renamed the same day, because quantities.json's `quantum_efficiency` note ruled that THE CURVE IS NOT AN ENTRY AND THERE IS NO FIELD FOR ONE, and listed the legal shapes: a scalar, points a PERSON read as one entry each with the wavelength pinned, or a vendor numeric table beside the other tables. This is the second shape and always was -- one value, `validity.wavelength` pinned to 600 nm, read by a person and not by a model, which is what keeps it out of 5.3's E6. What was wrong was the identifier: a reader greping the store would have found a name promising a curve. That is task 015's shape, a claim living in an entry name where nothing checks it, and it is why the id moved rather than the content. Nothing cited it -- checked before renaming -- and the claim is unchanged, so this is a rename and not a supersede; rule 8 keeps a replaced CLAIM, and no claim was replaced. THE CURVE IS NOT RESCALED AND THAT REFUSAL IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY. It peaks at 0.97 while the Kinetix22's own datasheet states 0.95, and the source declined to normalise one to the other because, in its words, the 2 per cent gap sits well inside the error of reading a graph by eye, so normalising the peak `would imply a precision neither source has` and would break traceability back to the Kinetix graph. THAT IS CARRIED HERE SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT DO THE ARITHMETIC THE SOURCE DECLINED TO DO. Scaling this curve by 0.95/0.97 produces a number with five figures of apparent agreement and no more evidence than it started with. IT IS THE WRONG BODY'S GRAPH, and that is a substitution the caller is making, not a fact this entry establishes. The two cameras share a sensor family and differ in array size; whether their QE curves coincide is not something either datasheet says. The same shape as the polystyrene plates standing in for beads. IT IS NOT camera_qe_peak. That entry is the Kinetix22's own documented 0.95 at E3 vendor_spec and survives if this curve is withdrawn; this one is a borrowed graph at E3 prior_run. They are separate files because they have different sources, different subjects and different failure modes, and because the source itself keeps them apart. WHAT WOULD RAISE IT: a real digitisation of the Kinetix22's own QE curve, which the source names as the action that would let it set `qe_verified: true` -- asking Photometrics for the curve as CSV. That is an action outside this repository. Slot: A1. Rule passed: 10.3 rule 1.
